title: North Korea Codifies Decentralized Nuclear Command Authority in Constitutional Amendment
summary: North Korea's constitutional amendments granted Kim Jong Un explicit nuclear forces command authority and introduced provisions for delegating nuclear launch authority to a national command-and-control organization, marking a significant shift in nuclear doctrine.
contents:
## North Korean Nuclear Command Restructuring

### Constitutional Nuclear Authority
North Korea's recently amended constitution granted the chairman of the State Affairs Commission explicit command authority over nuclear forces for the first time, according to the South Korean Ministry of Unification. Previous language vaguely referenced command over all armed forces of the state without specifically mentioning nuclear capabilities.

### Delegation Provisions
The amendment stated that the SAC chairman may delegate the authority to use nuclear forces to the national nuclear command-and-control organization. This represents a departure from North Korea's September 2022 nuclear policy law, which reiterated Kim Jong Un's sole authority without referencing any delegation mechanism.

### Strategic Rationale
Analysts assess the decentralized nuclear command-and-control structure targets South Korea's Three-Axis System, which includes the Kill Chain preemptive strike concept, Korea Air and Missile Defense, and Korea Massive Punishment and Retaliation. North Korea likely perceives centralized command as vulnerable to these offensive doctrines.

### Deterrence Implications
The constitutional change advances North Korea's efforts to project credible retaliatory capabilities by implying a more distributed decision-making structure. North Korean state media in May 2025 claimed military exercises ensured a command and mobilization system capable of rapidly responding to any nuclear escalation situation.

### Russian Influence
The modernization push coincides with deepening Russia-North Korea military cooperation. Russian Defense Minister Belousov met Kim in April to discuss future military cooperation plans, with a five-year military cooperation agreement planned for later in 2026.

title: NASA Psyche Spacecraft Completes Mars Flyby, Captures Stunning Images En Route to Metal-Rich Asteroid
summary: NASA's Psyche spacecraft completed its close approach of Mars on May 15, capturing thousands of images and receiving a 1,000 mph speed boost via gravity assist. The spacecraft now heads toward asteroid 16 Psyche, expected to arrive in summer 2029.
contents:
## Psyche Mars Flyby Achievement

### Mission Milestone
NASA's Psyche spacecraft completed its planned gravity assist flyby of Mars on May 15, 2026, passing within 2,864 miles (4,609 kilometers) of the planet's surface. The maneuver provided a critical 1,000 mile-per-hour speed boost and shifted the spacecraft's orbital plane by approximately 1 degree relative to the Sun.

### Imaging Campaign
The multispectral imager captured thousands of observations during the encounter, including unprecedented views of Mars from a high phase angle where the planet appeared as a thin crescent. The crescent appeared brighter and extended farther around the planet's disk than anticipated due to strong scattering of sunlight through the dusty Martian atmosphere.

### Instrument Calibration
All science instruments underwent calibration during the flyby, including magnetometers that may have detected Mars' bow shock, and the gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer. Multiple NASA and ESA missions provided complementary data for cross-calibration.

### Trajectory Confirmation
Navigation lead Don Han confirmed the spacecraft now travels on the correct trajectory for arrival at asteroid 16 Psyche in summer 2029. The 173-mile-wide metal-rich asteroid may represent an exposed planetary core, offering unprecedented insight into rocky planet interiors.

### Scientific Significance
Principal investigator Lindy Elkins-Tanton noted that the Mars flyby, anticipated for years, gave the spacecraft a critical gravitational slingshot farther into the solar system toward the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

title: Putin Arrives in Beijing for Xi Summit Days After Trump Visit, Showcasing China-Russia Alignment
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing Tuesday for his 25th visit to China, meeting Xi Jinping days after the Chinese leader hosted Trump. The summit covers Ukraine, the Iran war, energy cooperation, and their shared vision for a multipolar world order.
contents:
## Putin-Xi Beijing Summit

### Diplomatic Choreography
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing on May 20, 2026, for a state visit carefully calibrated to showcase China-Russia alignment amid global geopolitical upheaval. The visit came less than a week after Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump, underscoring Beijing's emergence as a focal point of global diplomacy.

### Summit Agenda
Xi and Putin planned discussions covering trade, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, energy cooperation including the Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline, and their aligned worldview. The leaders prepared to sign a declaration on establishing a multipolar world and a new type of international relations, according to Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov.

### Strategic Context
Putin's 25th visit to China occurred as Russia faces mounting battlefield losses in Ukraine, with Western estimates placing Russian casualties at 30,000 to 40,000 killed and wounded per month. China's purchases of Russian oil and exports of dual-use goods remain critical for Moscow's war effort, creating an increasingly lopsided relationship.

### Xi's Remark on Ukraine
During talks with Trump the previous week, Xi reportedly remarked that Putin might one day regret invading Ukraine, reflecting shifting battlefield dynamics where Ukraine achieved net territorial gains in 2026 through innovative drone warfare.

### Iran Dimensions
Both China and Russia maintain close partnerships with Tehran, raising questions about their potential role in mediating the US-Iran conflict. The Strait of Hormuz crisis continues driving energy cooperation between Moscow and Beijing.

title: Kim Jong Un Convenes Unprecedented Meeting of All Military Commanders, Orders Southern Border Fortification
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un summoned all commanding officers of brigade and division-level units on May 17, marking the first such meeting since he took power. Kim emphasized modernizing training methods and strengthening forces along the southern border.
contents:
## Kim Jong Un Military Commanders Summit

### Unprecedented Gathering
Kim Jong Un convened commanding officers of all Korean People's Army brigade and division-level units on May 17, 2026, according to North Korean state media reports on May 18. The meeting marked the first time Kim openly summoned operational commanders at this level since assuming power, with an estimated 180 to 250 officers attending from army, navy, air force, and strategic forces.

### Modernization Directives
Kim emphasized the need to update military training systems in line with modern warfare developments and advances in North Korean military equipment. Analysts interpret this as an effort to integrate lessons from the Ukraine conflict, where North Korean forces have observed frontline operations, particularly the effectiveness of drone warfare.

### Border Fortification
Kim referenced North Korea's territorial defense policy to strengthen first-line troops guarding the southern border and make it an impregnable fortress. This aligns with ongoing plans to deploy 250 new tactical ballistic missile launchers, three battalions of 155mm self-propelled artillery in the front area, and fortify positions north of the Military Demarcation Line.

### Constitutional Context
The meeting followed North Korea's constitutional amendments removing all references to reunification and establishing territorial provisions. The amendments codified Kim's designation of South Korea as North Korea's principal enemy and granted explicit nuclear command authority to the SAC chairman.

### Regional Implications
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed close monitoring of North Korean military movements in the MDL area while maintaining a solid readiness posture. The Ministry of Unification stated the government's goal of peaceful coexistence remains unshaken.
